events.title: Trinity's capture turns into a massacre
events.summary: A four-officer squad breaches Room 303 in the fire-gutted Heart O' The City Hotel and the Big Cop barks Trinity into surrender; she complies slowly and lets them believe the arrest is done. Outside, the Lieutenant waves off Agents Smith, Brown, and Jones as a jurisdiction grab and boasts that his two units are bringing her down, only for Smith to inform him the men are already dead. Back in the room, the moment the Big Cop reaches with the cuffs, Trinity explodes: she breaks the Big Cop, takes a
events.action: gun, and in a few seconds of panicked gunfire leaves every officer dead and herself the sole one standing, before a single dropped curse over the bodies.

affects_outside.enables: The squad's annihilation confirms Smith's warning and clears the way for the Agents to take the operation from the police, since the Lieutenant's men are gone and his authority is now hollow.
affects_outside.blocks_or_costs: It costs the police two units and then the entire Room 303 squad, and it ends any chance of containing Trinity by conventional force — the target walks away while the operation collapses.
affects_outside.off_screen_reactor: The Lieutenant, who staked his authority on his men 'bringing her down now,' is the off-screen counterpoint: Smith's flat correction that they are already dead undercuts his bluster even before the full scale of the loss is known to him.

events.title: Trinity's escape across the rooftops to the phone
events.summary: Told her hardline is cut and Agents are in the building, Trinity abandons her planned exit and runs for a phone at Wells and Lake on Morpheus's word. She slips past Agent Brown in the hall onto the fire escape, is forced upward when Agent Smith blocks the alley, and crosses the rooftops with impossible grace that Brown matches exactly. She dives through a lit window into a back stairwell, crashes down bleeding but on her feet, finds no pursuer behind her, and finally races a garbage truck to a街头

state_triples.reading: Trinity's discipline is the through-line: the same self-regulation that turns her panic into a soldier's obedience in the hotel is what lets her face a 40-foot gap with a perfectly calm face and then race a truck into a phone booth. What the accumulated scenes make visible is that her competence is real but not sovereign — every 'choice' is Morpheus's instruction or an Agent's blockade, and her cleanest physical win is the exact moment the net closes around someone else. She experiences survival; the event delivers the crew's exposure.

events.summary: In his apartment, Neo's computer types messages at him on its own and a real knock answers the last one, leaving him unable to trust cause and effect; he completes a disk deal with Choi and Dujour, then, spotting a white rabbit pin on Dujour's jacket, abandons his refusal and goes out with them. events.title: The Agents seize Neo at the office
events.summary: Guided by Morpheus over a cell phone, Neo flees the office floor as the Agents close in, but his nerve fails at the window ledge and he climbs back inside, walking straight into their hands. They take him in cuffs and march him out to a waiting sedan while Trinity watches the arrest from her motorcycle and curses what she sees.
events.action: Morpheus phones Neo a warning that pursuers are coming and directs his escape step by step through the office; Neo hides, slips past a cop, and reaches an empty office with a scaffold route to the roof. When Morpheus offers only the scaffold or enemy custody, Neo refuses the climb, then commits and steps onto the ledge, only to be knocked off balance by the wind, lose the phone, and retreat back inside, where a cop's arrival seals him. The Agents take him, handcuff him, and force him into the sedan as Trinity looks on helplessly.

state_triples.reading: She is the story's smallest and most unsettling betrayal: a single turned finger that hands Neo over, legible to everyone in the room yet opaque in motive. The scenes keep her unreadable on purpose, so that the moment stands for how ordinary the machinery of capture can be — a coworker, a gesture, and a life upended, with no way to know whether it was malice or mere reflex.

state_triples.reading: He is the last breath of Neo's ordinary world — a flat, courteous transaction that is chilling only in hindsight, because the package he hands over is the instrument of the escape that is about to fail. His blankness matters: the story lets the mundane delivery and the lethal pursuit occupy the same instant, so that the moment Neo's normal life ends is also the moment a stranger wishes him a nice day and means nothing by it.

state_triples.reading: The softpak is the ordinary wrapper around the extraordinary: a mundane delivery that becomes a lifeline the instant it is opened, then drops away once the phone has done its work. It marks the last ordinary object Neo will handle as a free man, and its disposability after the reveal underlines how the everyday has been hollowed out and repurposed by the pursuit.

state_triples.reading: The phone is the thread tying Neo to Morpheus, and its loss is the story's cleanest signal that he is now on his own: the moment the wind takes it from his hand is the moment guidance stops and the choice — and the failure — become entirely his. Falling into the void, it enacts the very thing Neo cannot yet grasp, that the world he trusts his body about is not the one he is actually in.

state_triples.reading: The window is the frame through which the story swaps one world for another: opened on Morpheus's word, it reveals not an exit but a vertiginous drop that Neo's body reads as death. It is the threshold he cannot cross, the literal edge of his disbelief, and every protest he makes is aimed at the space beyond it.

state_triples.reading: The scaffold is the exit that requires belief: Morpheus vouches for it, but to Neo it reads only as an impossible gap, and his refusal of it is the refusal of the whole leap the story will later demand of him. It stands, unused, as the road not taken — the proof that knowing the way out is not the same as being able to walk it.

state_triples.reading: The ledge is where the whole event turns: it is a short climb to Morpheus and a death sentence to Neo, and the gap between those two readings is the entire argument the story will spend itself closing. Neo steps onto it, says he is going to die, and climbs back — the first and most concrete demonstration that his prison is what he believes about the world, not the world itself.

state_triples.reading: The roof is the freedom Neo cannot reach, the far side of a test he fails. It matters only as the destination of the route he refuses, the concrete image of the escape that his disbelief costs him, and it stays above him, unreached, for the whole rest of the capture.

affects_outside.enables: Neo's capture puts him directly into the Agents' hands, which is what makes the interrogation and the choice of the red pill possible — the whole awakening sequence depends on him being taken rather than getting clean away.
affects_outside.blocks_or_costs: It costs Neo his last chance to escape on his own terms and strips him of Morpheus's guidance at the moment he most needs it, and it costs the resistance its operative-in-progress, leaving Trinity watching helplessly from the street.
affects_outside.off_screen_reactor: Morpheus, who has invested in this extraction and now loses Neo to custody, must respond to a failed rescue he could not prevent from a distance; his next moves are shaped by that loss.

events.boundary_reason: Morpheus's warning call (sc-017) triggers Neo's flight through the office and onto the ledge (sc-018), which resolves in his capture and forced entry into the sedan (sc-019); the question of whether he escapes the closing Agents is answered by his being taken, and Trinity's distant reaction closes the beat.
